summary: Hartford, Oxford County, Maine lookout: a 1918 Agamenticus tower was raised to 40 ft on Bear Mountain in 1934; removed 1950-1961; the register lists the site as gone.

facts.design: Steel tower moved from Mount Agamenticus, lengthened by a 15-foot extension
facts.status_note: Dismantled and removed between 1950 and 1961; no source describes the site today

events.note: Original steel tower erected on Mount Agamenticus; dismantled in 1934 and re-erected on Bear Mountain
Tower dismantled at Agamenticus, given a 15-foot extension to 40 ft, and erected on Bear Mountain in Hartford
Lewiston Civilian Conservation Corps crew did road work on the road to the tower (catalog places it near Waterford)
Dismantled and removed at some point between 1950 and 1961; the register gives a range, so 1961 is the latest possible year
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 annual report, the marker and the FFLOS register all say Hartford; the 1935 Maine Memory catalog says Waterford. We follow Hartford, but the Waterford entry is not explained by any source read.

notes_for_editor: Brief had no height or design; added from the 1934 report (40 ft). No source found on staffing, fires or the site today. Facebook posts by the FFLA Maine chapter show the tower in the 1950s but could not be read, so not cited. The 1934 annual report is read through its quotation on Forest Lookouts [2]; the report itself was not opened.
